core.title: Reference user/system flow prerequisites in the user/system flow URN shape
core.given: A user/system flow's plan artifact exists or is being authored, edited, reviewed or validated, with or without existing dependency entries
core.when: The planner writes, changes or checks that user/system flow's dependencies
core.then: Every entry in the user/system flow's dependencies must be a reference to a prerequisite user/system flow, written in the user/system flow URN shape given by the profile.
prefer: Foundation (commons) user/system flows often precede the user/system flows that build on them; order them first when that applies — a frequent pattern, not an unconditional requirement.
avoid: A data-flow consumer user/system flow that does not depend on the user/system flow producing the data it consumes — consumers must depend on producers.
Circular dependencies between user/system flows — direct, transitive, or a user/system flow listing itself — are forbidden.
Free-text, bare-id or references to finer-grained plan artifacts (such as product capabilities) in the dependencies list instead of a user/system flow reference in the user/system flow URN shape.
Reversing direction: making a producer depend on its consumer.
core.why: A dependency is a prerequisite user/system flow reference; one uniform user/system flow reference shape lets tooling resolve ordering, consumers need their producers first, and a cycle makes the user/system flows impossible to sequence.
evidence: Every entry in each user/system flow's dependencies matches the profile's user/system flow URN shape and resolves to an existing user/system flow.
A graph walk over all user/system flow dependencies (including self-edges) finds no cycle.
Each consumer user/system flow lists the user/system flow producing its consumed data among its dependencies; no producer depends on its consumer.
verification: Treat every dependency entry as a prerequisite-user/system-flow reference and validate it against the profile's user/system flow URN shape; an entry that does not match, or does not resolve to an existing user/system flow, is a violation.
Validate existing entries on every user/system flow, not only on user/system flows changed in the current edit; a user/system flow referencing itself is a cycle of length one.

The reference-shape check and the whole-graph cycle walk (self-edges included) are mechanical; the consumer-depends-on-producer (data-flow) check is llm_judged unless the stack's plan data records train-level produce/consume relationships.

values: user/system flow spec added or edited
user/system flow dependency list added or edited
dependency reference not matching the user/system flow reference shape
consumer user/system flow missing dependency on its producer user/system flow

fires: Planner authors a new user/system flow that needs another user/system flow's outputs or foundation first
Planner edits the dependencies list of an existing user/system flow
Planner adds or edits a user/system flow that consumes data produced by another user/system flow
Planner reviews or validates existing user/system flow specs, including ones whose dependencies list contains malformed references, a self-reference, or a cycle
Planner edits any part of a user/system flow spec whose existing dependencies violate the reference shape or form a cycle
doesNotFire: Editing a product capability's internal acceptances or DESIRED OUTCOMES without touching or reviewing any user/system flow spec
Authoring documentation or plans that do not define, edit or validate user/system flow specs

profileRequirements.meaning: The URN shape every prerequisite-user/system-flow reference must match — the core's 'user/system flow URN shape' in then, avoid, evidence and the check.
The concrete plan-artifact kinds this rule fires on: the kind that defines a user/system flow and the registry kind that lists user/system flows.

neutralityNotes: User/system flows, product capabilities and DESIRED OUTCOMES are ATDD plan-artifact vocabulary present in the closed profile vocabulary (urn.user-system-flow, urn.capability, urn.desired-outcome, layout.capability_dir), so the core uses them rather than code roles; no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path is named. The only genuinely stack-specific datum is the concrete reference form user-system-flow:{user_system_flow_id} / ^user-system-flow:[0-9]{2}-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$, which becomes profile data (urn.user-system-flow); a stack with a different user/system flow URN shape realizes the identical obligation with its own value. The two concrete source examples (verifier_detail[1], verifier_detail[2]) stay Bun-only under the reference-example policy. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and remains empty in the core. bun.json declares no per-rule severity or disposition, so none was invented; the llm_judged status of the consumer→producer check and the validate-every-user/system-flow scope are kept in core.verification.
